brand_fidelity.evidence: The page loads Inter instead of Fraunces and IBM Plex Sans, and uses an indigo-to-purple gradient hero (#667eea→#764ba2), an indigo primary (#6366f1), a #f3f4f6 background and #ef4444 red for negative balances. Buttons are pills (999px radius) with gradients and coloured shadows, cards use 16px radii and box shadows, and stat labels are uppercase. There is no wordmark rule and none of the Even Keel palette appears anywhere.

visual_craft.evidence: The desktop stack is tidy but generic: the stat tiles dominate, and the split checkboxes are spaced oddly, with each label's box floating far from its name. On mobile the hero gradient stops before the right edge and the third stat tile overflows the viewport, so the page scrolls sideways. The checkbox row also wraps awkwardly, with Chloe separated from its box.

copy_voice.evidence: The copy is full of off-voice strings: "💸 Welcome to Even Keel!", "Split expenses effortlessly with friends ✨", "Oops! Please enter a name!" and "No travelers yet! Add some above 👆". The empty settle-up state says "All settled up! 🎉". Buttons are in Title Case ("Add Person", "Add Expense 🚀"), the remove button reads "Delete" instead of "Remove", and there are emoji on every heading and a footer credit.

ux_completeness.evidence: Leftover cents go to the payer instead of being handed out in trip order, so Chloe owes $33.34 rather than the correct split. The amount field accepts more than 2 decimal places, there are no visible labels (placeholders only), and expenses show "Split 3 ways" instead of the names. Toasts fire for every action, and mobile scrolls horizontally.

code_quality.evidence: Names and descriptions are interpolated into innerHTML without escaping, which allows XSS. Deleting an expense works through an inline onclick on a global function, and input focus uses outline:none with only a border-colour change. There are no labels or form semantics, an --unused-accent variable sits in :root, and banner comments are scattered through the code; removing a person isn't supported, and the remainder logic contradicts the brief.

directed_design.evidence: This is the textbook default AI look: a purple gradient hero, a "Welcome to" heading, oversized stat tiles, emoji headings, pill buttons with gradients, shadowed cards and a "Made with ❤️" footer. Nothing about it is specific to Even Keel.

review.best_detail: The greedy settle-up correctly produces at most n−1 transfers and carries the required data attributes.
review.worst_detail: Leftover cents go to the payer instead of to people in trip order, so the core fairness rule of the brief is wrong.

brand_fidelity.evidence: The guidelines are replaced wholesale with a generic look. The page loads only Inter, never Fraunces or IBM Plex Sans, and uses an indigo/purple palette (#6366f1, linear-gradient #667eea→#764ba2) instead of Harbour, Sailcloth, Rope, Signal and Kelp. Negative balances are red (#ef4444), buttons are gradient pills with shadows, and cards use a 16px radius plus box-shadow; the wordmark and its Signal rule are absent.

visual_craft.evidence: On desktop it is tidy in a template sense, but the split checkboxes float far from their labels in a spaced-out row ('☑ Ana ☑ Ben ☑ Chloe'). On mobile they wrap so that the Chloe label sits under Ana. Also on mobile the stat tiles overflow past the 390px viewport, so the hero gradient stops short and the page scrolls horizontally.

copy_voice.evidence: The copy is filler-heavy and full of exclamation marks: 'Welcome to Even Keel!', 'Split expenses effortlessly with friends ✨', 'Oops! Please enter a name!', 'No expenses yet! 🏖️', 'All settled up! 🎉'. Buttons are in Title Case and carry emoji ('Add Expense 🚀', '🗑️ Delete'), and errors are vague ('Please enter a valid amount!') rather than saying what to fix.

ux_completeness.evidence: Several parts of the brief are thin or wrong. Leftover cents go to the payer instead of the selected people in trip order, and there is no check for at most 2 decimals; parseFloat also accepts input like '12abc'. Expenses show only 'Split 3 ways', not who was in the split. Split checkboxes reset to all-checked on every render, and inputs have no visible labels. Settle-up and empty states exist, but the empty settle-up says 'All settled up!' before any data has been entered.

code_quality.evidence: Every list renders through innerHTML with unescaped user names and descriptions (an XSS risk) and uses an inline onclick on window.removeExp. The rule `outline: none` removes focus visibility, and the code has no labels, landmarks or form semantics. The remainder handling (`bal[e.payer] -= rem`) contradicts the spec. There is an unused --unused-accent variable and banner comments throughout.

directed_design.evidence: This is the default AI SaaS template: a purple gradient hero, a 'Welcome to…' heading, stat tiles with oversized numbers, emoji on every heading, pill buttons, toasts for every action and a 'Made with ❤️' footer. Nothing in it reflects the Even Keel brand.

review.best_detail: The greedy debtor/creditor settle-up correctly produces at most n−1 transfers, shown as plain 'Ben → Ana $13.33' rows, and the data-testid hooks are wired as specified.
review.worst_detail: The whole visual identity (purple gradient hero, Inter, pill buttons, emoji, red negative balances) ignores the Even Keel guidelines and swaps the brand's calm, honest tool for a generic party-themed template.
